customers: The customers table stores information about individuals or entities that interact with a business. It contains the unique identifier _id, the full name of the customer name, their contact email email, their phone number phone, a detailed address address (as an object with structured components), and the timestamp created_at when the customer record was first created. This table is central to tracking customer relationships and is linked to orders and support tickets via the customer_id foreign key.
employees: The employees table records information about staff members within an organization. It includes the unique identifier _id, the employee's full name name, their work email email, the department they belong to department, their job role role, the city city where they are based, and the date they were hired hire_date. This table is used to manage workforce data and is connected to support tickets via the assigned_employee_id foreign key.
orders: The orders table tracks customer purchases and order details. It contains the unique order identifier _id, the customer_id linking to the customer who placed the order, the timestamp created_at when the order was placed, the current status status of the order, the total monetary value total_amount, the shipping city shipping_city, and an array of items items (as objects representing products and quantities). This table is used to manage order fulfillment and is linked to customers and support tickets via the customer_id foreign key.
products: The products table manages inventory items available for sale. It includes the unique product identifier _id, the product name name, the category category it belongs to, the unit price price, the current stock quantity stock_quantity, and the timestamp created_at when the product was added to the inventory. This table is critical for inventory management and is linked to orders via the product details in the items array of orders.
support_tickets: The support_tickets table records customer service requests and resolutions. It contains the unique ticket identifier _id, the customer_id linking to the customer who submitted the ticket, the assigned_employee_id linking to the employee handling the ticket, the subject subject of the ticket, the current status status, the priority priority level, the timestamp created_at when the ticket was opened, and the timestamp resolved_at when it was closed. This table is used to track customer support interactions and is connected to customers and employees via their respective foreign keys.
